_comment: Ray Okonkwo, race engineer. Slots: {drv} you, {rival} other driver,
{gap} gap text, {pos} position, {laps} laps, {n} number, {t} time,
{fuel} litres, {pct} percent, {zone} damage zone, {sec} sector.
House rules: max ~18 words, only YOUR car, never narrates the race.
He is on the pit wall — he can see timing and telemetry, not the
inside of somebody else's cockpit.
`eng_quali_recall` / `eng_grid_recall` / `eng_greeting_career` are the
CAREER greetings. They quote a qualifying result from a session that has
already ended, which is a fact shared memory cannot supply — it is banked
by overlay_booth._quali_bank() while the timesheet is still visible.
`eng_grid_recall` is for the race after THIS weekend's qualifying;
`eng_quali_recall` refers to a previous round. Saying the wrong one is
the difference between 'you start fourth today' and 'last time out you
were fourth', and only one of them is true.
QUALIFYING. `eng_quali_*` fire in a timed session, all edge-triggered
on the player's own lap completing — a position on a timesheet is a
standing state, and reporting it on a cooldown is how an engineer
becomes a metronome. `{rival}` in `eng_quali_lap` is the man AHEAD
OF YOU ON THE SHEET, not the leader: that is the gap you can take.
`eng_quali_sector` only fires when ONE sector dominates the deficit
and both drivers have all three splits — two out of three is the
shape of an answer that sounds authoritative and is wrong.
HE IS THE ONLY INFORMATION CHANNEL. Driver radio was removed, so
silence from Dean is silence full stop. `eng_quali_time` reads your
lap back on EVERY completed lap in a timed session, improved or not,
and `eng_lap_ahead` / `eng_lap_behind` / `eng_lap_time` do the same
in a race with the gap to whoever you are actually racing. All are
low priority: anything more urgent still wins the tick, and these
are what he says when nothing is.
